Visual scores

Orbit rave

P(u) = ((1.8+0.58cos5u)cos3u,
(1.8+0.58cos5u)sin3u, 0.58sin5u)

Geometry and musical score

A 3:5 torus braid rotates in perspective. Two heads traverse it at different rates. Their vertical coordinates select Dorian scale degrees; every audible lead attack lights its exact braid position. The slower voice answers the faster voice. A sparse opening grows into interlocking arpeggios and a syncopated bass groove. Formula u is in radians; event positions store u/(2π). Scan progress t runs from 0 to 1. The seed fixes geometry and transposition. Every visible note flash uses the corresponding event onset and position. Four independently weighted layers supply lead, answer, bass and percussion. Pitch f=130.81·2^(n/12), with scale intervals (0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10). Vivid uses the event instruments, short beat-related echoes and a soft mix knee; Original keeps the legacy pitch-curve voice. All dry notes end before t=0.985. The artwork follows the score clock, so pausing and restarting preserve alignment.

Prism break

Geometry and musical score

A triangular iterated-function construction is reflected into six sectors. A base-three address identifies each illuminated cell and its pitch; more address digits reveal smaller triangles. Six mirrored copies flash together on the same note. A clipped FM pluck answers a glass voice over a broken bass rhythm; the third section adds a faster high-register run. Vertices Vᵢ are (0,0), (0.94,−0.53), (0.94,0.53). Sₖ reflects y for odd k and is the identity for even k. Scan progress t runs from 0 to 1. The seed fixes geometry and transposition. Fractal drop

P_child = P+ℓ(cosθ,sinθ)
ℓ_child = 0.72ℓ; θ_child = θ±α

Geometry and musical score

A seven-level binary tree is generated recursively. Branch depth and left/right address choose notes. Internal branches grow first; leaf notes cascade after the midpoint as the bass and half-time drums arrive. A note travels along its own branch and rings at its tip. The final tree remains visible. Branch angle is seeded. This is a recursive geometric score, not a biological growth model. Seeded branch angle α=0.436 radians; initial length 0.73. Scan progress t runs from 0 to 1. Euclid’s carousel

E(k,n,j) = 1 if (k(j−ρ) mod n) < k
(k,n) = (3,8), (5,12), (7,16)

Geometry and musical score

Three rhythm wheels distribute 3, 5 and 7 attacks across 8, 12 and 16 subdivisions of the same bar. The outer wheel carries a recurring melody; the middle answers in wood tones; the inner plays bass. The sweep crosses exactly the node that triggers each note. Filled nodes and their polygon show the attack pattern. Rotation offsets ρ and key are seeded. The final tonic is an extra cadence attack. The bass wheel enters after the opening bar. Root=116.541 Hz; equal-tempered pitch f=root·2^(n/12), scale intervals=(0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10). The straight score clock is t=0.018+0.014j. Spirograph shuffle delays every second eighth to 5/8 of its quarter. Geometry, key and event score are deterministic from the seed. Vivid plays the event instruments and Original uses the legacy pitch voices. Both scan speeds scale the same normalized timeline. All dry notes finish by t=0.985.

Spirograph shuffle

A soft whistle melody and glass replies follow a 5:3 swung subdivision clock, with walking bass and brush accents. The second half changes register before a short tonic answer. Paper dragon groove

D₀ = []; Dₙ₊₁ = Dₙ ⊕ [1] ⊕ (−reverse Dₙ)
Pⱼ₊₁ = Pⱼ+(cosθⱼ,sinθⱼ)

Geometry and musical score

Ten recursive paperfolding expansions produce 1023 quarter turns and a 1024-segment dragon curve. Here ⊕ concatenates turn lists and θ advances by ±π/2. A moving cursor unfolds the curve. Local fold direction offsets a recurring minor-pentatonic hook; alternate segments trade FM plucks and crystal replies. A broken beat becomes denser in the third bar, then leaves room for the ending. Root=146.832 Hz; equal-tempered pitch f=root·2^(n/12), scale intervals=(0, 3, 5, 7, 10). The straight score clock is t=0.018+0.014j. Rubber-band ballet

yᵢ(s,t) = Σₙ₌₁⁵ Aᵢₙ(t)sin(nπs)
Aᵢₙ = Σₑ gₑ sin(nπaₑ)sin(28πnτₑ)e^(−τₑ/0.055)/n

Geometry and musical score

Five fixed-end strings form a pentagram and are tuned to a major-pentatonic scale. Each lead event plucks its selected string at position a, and the visual displacement perpendicular to each string sums five damped sine modes. τ is normalized time since that event. Each string joins vertex i to vertex i+2 of a regular pentagon; the display scales normalized displacement by 0.17 times the vertex radius. The displayed wave motion is slowed for readability, not an audio-frequency oscilloscope. The sound uses fractional-delay plucked-string synthesis, an interlocking high reply, syncopated bass and dry rim taps. A repeating hook gains a second voice after the first bar. Root=164.814 Hz; equal-tempered pitch f=root·2^(n/12), scale intervals=(0, 2, 4, 7, 9). The straight score clock is t=0.018+0.014j. Spirograph shuffle delays every second eighth to 5/8 of its quarter. Geometry, key and event score are deterministic from the seed. Vivid plays the event instruments and Original uses the legacy pitch voices. Both scan speeds scale the same normalized timeline. All dry notes finish by t=0.985.

Construction references

  • Wolfram: torus parameterization
  • Georgi: The Physics of Waves, section 11.3
  • Wolfram: moire construction
  • Toussaint: The Euclidean Algorithm Generates Traditional Musical Rhythms
  • Wolfram: Circle Rolling Inside Another
  • MIT: Vibration Analysis by Mode Superposition

The torus surface is restricted to a winding curve. The nodal artwork uses the antisymmetric cosine-mode combination, with artistic morphs between mode pairs; it is not a center-driven physical plate model. The prism and tree use the explicit recursive maps above. The moire field multiplies two slowly rotated gratings. The musical sequences, event mappings, rendering and timbres are original app constructions.
